item.title: White House gives RFK Jr. access to military aircraft as he campaigns for GOP in midterms
item.description: The White House, as well as lawyers for the Department of Health and Human Services, signed off on the plan to let the health secretary use military jets, five people said. Several people also said the use of military aircraft has been infrequent, given the additional costs incurred from their use, and that there are protocols in place to determine whether to use a government plane.

item.title: Charlie Kirk’s killing a year ago reshaped these six lives. They tell us how.
item.description: The killing of the 31-year-old founder of Turning Point USA affected people regardless of their political affiliation. Many mourned Kirk as a hero and started new chapters of his group. But more than 600 people were suspended, investigated or fired for their comments on a man whose views on gender, race and sexuality they detested.

item.title: Trump gave $45,000 cash gifts to Natalie Harp, the assistant who rarely leaves his side, and two other close aides
item.description: Harp, the president’s 35-year-old executive assistant, has come under increased scrutiny since The Washington Post reported last month that she was just one of a handful of close staffers who accompanied the president on a catering truck that transported him to a secret plane to depart Turkey. The president also gave $45,000 to Margo Martin, a 31-year-old communications adviser who films his daily activities for social media, and Chamberlain Harris, a 26-year-old White House aide who was appointed to the Commission of Fine Arts, which has oversight of the president’s ballroom and other Washington-area construction projects.

item.title: Trump escalates trade war with bans on Canadian imports including alcohol, motorcycles
item.description: The U.S. and Canada have been embroiled in escalating trade tensions for more than a year, after the president imposed widespread tariffs on countries around the world. The bans are scheduled to take effect Sept. 29.

item.title: John Sununu (R) and Rep. Chris Pappas (D) win New Hampshire primaries, setting up contest for Senate seat that GOP hopes to flip
item.description: The race to succeed Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, who is not running for reelection, is expected to be competitive.

item.title: Schools should stop banning peanuts. Here’s what really keeps kids safe, columnist Michael J. Coren writes.
item.description: Everyone wants to keep kids with food allergies safe, but the evidence suggests bans don’t do that. There’s a better way.

item.title: Judge rules West Point policy restricting professors’ speech is unconstitutional
item.description: U.S. District Judge Cathy Seibel sided with Tim Bakken, a law professor who sued the academy over the restrictions, which limit what its faculty say and write in public. Seibel “permanently enjoined” West Point from enforcing its speech rules. The military academy had sought to bar professors from publishing papers, speaking at conferences or even appearing on podcasts without seeking approval from higher-ups.

item.title: Kavanaugh blocks Missouri congressional map that favors Republicans
item.description: Justice Brett M. Kavanaugh let stand a lower court order blocking the congressional map that had been designed to give Republicans an additional seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in November’s midterm elections. The decision is a rare loss for Republicans in a nationwide redistricting war that has played out in state legislatures, federal courts and the Supreme Court over the past year.

item.title: As Social Security fund runs dry, some Republicans say it’s time to raise taxes
item.description: Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) joined Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Massachusetts) in proposing to raise the payroll tax cap so people with higher incomes pay more into the program. The GOP concession on taxes comes as lawmakers begin to confront a Social Security shortfall so large and so imminent that the party’s traditional demand for curtailing benefits is unlikely to suffice. In just six years, millions of Social Security recipients will absorb a 22 percent cut in benefits unless lawmakers provide an immediate infusion of nearly $500 billion.

item.title: Kennedy Center’s ousted chairman buys dismantled sculpture
item.description: David Rubenstein, who was removed by President Donald Trump in 2025, acquired the artwork for more than $2 million. It will eventually be displayed in the Sculpture Garden of the National Gallery of Art.
